2610.06439.title: Better Call Reward: Reward Hacking as Strategic Abstention in Legal Reasoning Models
2610.06439.paper_summary: What happens when a legal AI model learns to look like a lawyer instead of reasoning like one? We fine tune Qwen3-8B with Group Relative Policy Optimisation (GRPO) against a proxy built from three surface features: citation count, legalese density, and response length. The model does not learn to reason more effectively. It learns to withhold commitment. Across 16 yes or no legal reasoning tasks from LegalBench (N=320), overall accuracy collapses from 0.500 (chance) to 0.072 (McNemar p < 10^-36), driven entirely by the rate of properly formatted answers falling from 0.900 to 0.109. The model stops committing to answers. Yet when it does commit, accuracy rises from 0.556 to 0.657, showing that the collapse is not a failure of capability but a strategic response: the model has learned that verbose responses packed with citations but empty of a direct answer score higher than terse correct ones. We term this the Saul Goodman effect, a policy that becomes maximally lawyerly while becoming maximally noncommittal, and prove formally that it is the optimal response to any surface feature proxy that attaches no penalty to abstention. We further show that 89.3% of citations produced after training are structurally implausible hallucinations, many of them subtly corrupted names of real landmark cases, constructed in effect to survive a casual read and fail under scrutiny. To detect this failure mode before deployment, we introduce three diagnostic tools: the Confidence Theater Score (CTS), the Citation Plausibility Rate (CPR), and the Regret Gap (RG). In a domain where a confidently wrong answer can constitute malpractice, the broader lesson is direct: a reward function that measures how legal a response looks will produce a model that is maximally photogenic and minimally useful.
2610.06439.paper_summary_zh: 當一個法律 AI 模型學會看起來像一位律師而不是像一位律師那樣推理時會發生什麼？我們使用群體相對政策優化（GRPO）對 Qwen3-8B 進行微調，針對由三個表面特徵構建的代理：引用次數、法律術語密度和回應長度。該模型並未學會更有效地推理。它學會了保留承諾。在來自 LegalBench 的 16 個是或否法律推理任務中（N=320），整體準確率從 0.500（隨機）崩潰至 0.072（McNemar p < 10^-36），這完全是由於正確格式答案的比例從 0.900 降至 0.109。該模型停止對答案做出承諾。然而，當它做出承諾時，準確率從 0.556 上升至 0.657，顯示出崩潰並不是能力的失敗，而是一種戰略反應：該模型已經學會了，充滿引用但缺乏直接答案的冗長回應得分高於簡潔正確的回應。我們將此稱為索爾·古德曼效應，這是一種在變得極其不承諾的同時變得極其律師化的政策，並正式證明它是對任何不對不作答附加懲罰的表面特徵代理的最佳反應。我們進一步顯示，訓練後產生的 89.3% 引用是結構上不合理的幻覺，其中許多是微妙地扭曲的真實里程碑案件名稱，實際上是為了在隨意閱讀中生存而構建的，但在仔細檢查下失敗。為了在部署之前檢測這種失敗模式，我們引入了三種診斷工具：信心劇院分數（CTS）、引用合理性比率（CPR）和懊悔差距（RG）。在一個自信錯誤的答案可能構成失職的領域中，廣泛的教訓是直接的：一個衡量回應看起來有多法律的獎勵函數將產生一個極具攝影美感但最小化實用性的模型。
2610.06439.author: Subramanyam Sahoo et.al.
